thread:
Maya K: Hey @support, customer ran into SSO failures right after IdP pushed a metadata update. They say logins started failing with 'invalid_signature' and 'Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL mismatch'. They just rotated certs and also changed the ACS URL to include an extra unicode character at the end (looks like a zero-width joiner).
Tom R: Ugh unicode. Any chance the ACS in the SP config still has the old trailing slash?
Maya K: SP ACS configured as `https://app.customer.example/saml/acs` but IdP metadata now has `https://app.customer.example/saml/acs` (there's a weird invisible char). The customer didn't notice.
Juniper (Support): Thanks, Maya. Can you paste the raw IdP metadata blob? Also, any error lines from our SSO logs?
Maya K: Pasting relevant lines from logs:
```
2025-11-16T15:02:13Z SAML_ERROR InvalidSignature - Signature verification failed for Response id=abc123
2025-11-16T15:02:13Z SAML_WARN ACS URL mismatch: expected=https://app.customer.example/saml/acs actual=https://app.customer.example/saml/acs
2025-11-16T15:02:13Z SAML_DEBUG Certificate fingerprint in metadata: SHA1: aa:bb:cc:...  (new cert)
```
Tom R: Can the metadata parser normalise Unicode or strip control chars? Our parser currently trims whitespace but doesn't strip zero-width chars.
Oliver S: @Tom I tried a quick repro with the python-saml lib — it treats the `Location` attribute as literal. If there's a non-printing char, the string compare fails causing ACS mismatch before signature checks in some flows.
IdP Bot: Metadata fetch from https://idp.customer.example/metadata.xml succeeded (200). Last-modified: 2025-11-16T14:58:02Z.
Juniper (Support): Ok, next steps: 1) ask customer to temporarily patch IdP metadata to remove the invisible char; 2) show a quick workaround on our side (non-production) to relax strict ACS match; 3) escalate to eng to consider normalization in metadata ingestion.
Maya K: Customer says they can't edit metadata right now (managed by their central IdP team). They asked if we can accept the incoming ACS value in the meantime.
Tom R: Workaround idea: We can add a tolerant compare that strips Unicode category Cf (format) characters and zero-width spaces when matching ACS locations during runtime. That would be a small change but needs review (security concern: ACS matching loosening).
Oliver S: Yea security will flag relaxing match rules. Alternative: canonicalize both by normalizing Unicode (NFC) and removing Cf-range. Implementation note (python):
```
import unicodedata
import regex as re

def norm_for_compare(s):
    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s)
    # remove Unicode format chars (category Cf)
    return re.sub(r"\p{Cf}+", "", s)
```
Maya K: Could we add a temporary per-tenant config flag like `saml.relax_acs_unicode_normalization = true` so it's opt-in? Then customer enables it for their tenant until IdP fixes metadata.
Juniper (Support): That seems reasonable as long as it's opt-in and logged. I'll get permission from security.
Tom R: For immediate help, tell customer to re-upload metadata to our admin portal with sanitized copy. They can retrieve metadata, run simple normalization client-side and re-upload. Command we suggested to them to fetch + show characters: 
```
curl -s https://idp.customer.example/metadata.xml | od -An -t x1 | sed -n '1,2p'
```
It shows `ef bb bf` or `e2 80 8b` sequences for BOM / zero-width space.
Maya K: Customer tried `od` and found `e2 80 8b` at the end of the ACS URL. They said the IdP team applied a template that accidentally appended a zero-width space. They're opening a ticket with the IdP.
Juniper (Support): Good. Security approved a temporary opt-in flag as long as we: 1) require tenant admin to enable it, 2) log any normalized matches, 3) auto-disable after 7 days unless the tenant requests extension. Can eng prototype this?
Tom R: I can put together a small patch: on metadata ingestion / at runtime ACS check, call `norm_for_compare()` on both sides. I will add an audit log entry like: `SAML_ACS_NORMALIZED_MATCH tenant=x, original_acs='...', normalized_acs='...'`
Oliver S: Test plan: unit tests with ACS values containing U+200B, BOM, NBSP etc; integration test with SAML Response where Location contains zero-width space; ensure signature verification still works because normalization only applies to compare of ACS strings, not the signed assertion data.
Maya K: Customer is asking for ETA. Any idea how long to roll opt-in?
Tom R: I can have a prototype PR today, review tomorrow, and if approved we can deploy to staging in 48h. Production rollout can be gated behind feature flag and tenant opt-in — maybe total 5 business days if no blocking reviews.
Juniper (Support): OK I'll tell customer the workaround (upload sanitized metadata or enable flag once available). Also I'll create ticket CS-9876 and link here.
Maya K: Also logging note — we should redact cert fingerprints in public logs. Right now fingerprint is present in debug lines.
Oliver S: Agreed. I'll make a separate follow-up PR to avoid leaking cert material in logs.
Juniper (Support): Updated ticket CS-9876 with steps, eng owner Tom R, SRE watch, and security approval for opt-in flag. Customer notified. :thumbsup: 
Maya K: Thanks team. If IdP pushes additional tweaks (they said they might change entityID encoding), we'll keep monitoring.
Tom R: I'll include a small runbook snippet for support: what to run to detect invisible chars, sample `python` one-liner: 
```
python - <<'PY'
import sys, unicodedata,regex as re
s=sys.stdin.read().strip()
print(re.sub(r"\p{Cf}+","",unicodedata.normalize('NFC',s)))
PY
```

Juniper (Support): Adding runbook note to internal KB under support/sso/runbooks. Closing thread here, feel free to reopen if customer can't update metadata.
